help.intro: A short text of about 130 words about German family names: Müller is the most common one, and it simply means miller, the man who makes flour. Schmidt is the smith, Schneider the tailor, Fischer the fisherman, Weber the weaver, Meyer the farm manager, Bäcker the baker. Most German surnames are old job titles, and the text explains why, with real numbers. You need what you have just learnt: job words and their feminine forms with -in (der Bäcker, die Bäckerin), simple compounds (Familienname = Familie + Name) and the verbs heißen, sein and machen. The questions ask what a name means and how many people carry it.
help.tips[0].title: Names that are jobs
help.tips[0].text: Müller = miller (Mühle = mill, Mehl = flour). Schmidt / Schmitt / Schmid = smith. Schneider = tailor (schneiden = to cut). Fischer = fisherman. Weber = weaver. Bäcker = baker. Koch = cook. Many German families got their name from the job of a man about seven hundred years ago. The job word is masculine; the woman gets -in: der Müller, die Müllerin; der Bäcker, die Bäckerin.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: The miller makes flour. Ms Müller, however, is a teacher.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Mr Fischer is not a fisherman. He is a doctor.
help.tips[0].check.q: What does the name Schneider mean?
help.tips[0].check.why: schneiden = to cut; the Schneider cuts cloth and makes clothes.
help.tips[1].title: Words built from two words
help.tips[1].text: German glues words together. The last part says what it is; the first part says which kind: Familienname = Familie + Name (family name), Vorname = vor + Name (first name), Hausnummer = Haus + Nummer. The last word gives the article: der Name, so der Familienname; die Nummer, so die Hausnummer.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: My first name is Anna, my family name is Müller.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The name is old, but the jobs are new.
help.tips[1].check.q: Familienname: which part gives the article?
help.tips[1].check.why: The last part of a compound decides the article.
help.remember[0]: Müller, Schmidt, Schneider, Fischer, Weber, Bäcker: old jobs that became names.
help.remember[1]: Compound = last part gives the meaning and the article: der Familienname, die Hausnummer.
help.exam: Short texts about names, jobs and families with multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: Why do so many Germans have the same name, and what does it mean? Read the story behind Müller, Schmidt and Schneider.
help.vocab[0].example: Müller ist der häufigste Familienname in Deutschland.
help.vocab[1].example: Vor siebenhundert Jahren haben die Menschen nur einen Vornamen.
passageTranslation:
In Germany very many people are called Müller. More than seven hundred thousand! Müller is the most common family name in Germany. In second place is Schmidt, in third Schneider. Then come Fischer, Weber and Meyer.

Why? The names are old. About seven hundred years ago people have only a first name: Hans, Peter, Anna. But in a village there are two or three men with the name Hans. What do you do? You say: Hans the miller. Hans the smith. Hans the fisherman. The job becomes the name.

The miller works in the mill and makes flour. The smith makes things from iron. The tailor makes clothes. The weaver makes cloth. The fisherman catches fish. The baker bakes bread.

Today Mr Müller is perhaps a doctor, and Ms Fischer is a teacher. The name is old, but the job is new.
questions[0].questionTranslation: How many people in Germany are called Müller?
questions[1].explanation: "Auf Platz zwei steht Schmidt, auf Platz drei Schneider."
questions[1].questionTranslation: Which name is in second place?
questions[2].explanation: "Vor etwa siebenhundert Jahren haben die Menschen nur einen Vornamen: Hans, Peter, Anna."
questions[2].questionTranslation: What do people have seven hundred years ago?
questions[3].explanation: "Aber in einem Dorf gibt es zwei oder drei Männer mit dem Namen Hans. Was macht man? Man sagt: Hans, der Müller."
questions[3].questionTranslation: Why does one say 'Hans the miller'?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: because there are several men called Hans in the village
questions[3].optionsTranslation[3]: because Müller is a beautiful and very old name for men
questions[4].explanation: "Der Müller arbeitet in der Mühle und macht Mehl."
questions[4].optionsTranslation[1]: He makes flour in the mill.
questions[5].explanation: "Der Schmied macht Dinge aus Eisen." The family name is Schmidt, the job is Schmied.
questions[6].explanation: "… und Frau Fischer ist Lehrerin." Lehrerin = female teacher (Lehrer + -in).
questions[7].explanation: "Der Name ist alt, aber der Beruf ist neu."
questions[7].questionTranslation: What does the last sentence say?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[0]: The names are new, the jobs are old.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: The names are old, the jobs are new.
